quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: In a longer phrase the small words are weak. Put all your attention on the stressed word and its vowel.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "peak": the vowel stayed long and tense before the /k/. "Pick" would be short and relaxed.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both vowels are front and high, but /ɪ/ sits slightly lower and more relaxed. The sound your ear catches first is the difference in length: /iː/ lasts noticeably longer.
quests.mouthPosition: Try saying /iː/ with a wide, tense smile, then relax the cheeks and shorten the sound; that slack, quick version is /ɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: It was a long trek to the village.
quests.hint: The stressed word carries the difference. Is its vowel half open or wide open?
quests.explanation: Here, "trek" had a half-open vowel and the jaw stayed high. "Track" drops the jaw wide.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The difference is jaw opening. /e/ keeps the mouth half open; /æ/ opens it wide so the vowel sounds fuller and broader.
quests.mouthPosition: Start from /e/, then lower the jaw another centimetre without moving the tongue tip from behind the lower teeth - that wide sound is /æ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a bump in the road.
quests.hint: Ignore the words around it. Was there a puff of air as the first sound was released?
quests.explanation: You heard "bump": the lips opened softly and the voice began at once. "Pump" would start with a clear breath.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The voiceless /p/ releases a burst of breath before the vowel; the voiced /b/ moves quickly into the vowel with the voice already on.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the lips together without tension. Push out air for /p/; let the voice begin for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how far the mouth opens at the start of the vowel.
quests.explanation: The word was "tile": the mouth opened wide and then closed. "Tale" starts half open and glides less.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /eɪ/ glides from a mid-front position up toward /ɪ/, while /aɪ/ starts with a wide-open mouth and glides up. The starting point differs: half-open for /eɪ/, fully open for /aɪ/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /aɪ/ open the jaw wide first, then close it. For /eɪ/ begin half open and close a short distance.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: At the end of a stressed word, check the vowel length as well as the ending.
quests.explanation: The word was "buzz": the vowel lasted longer and the ending was a soft buzz. "Bus" is shorter and ends with a sharp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the end of a word, /z/ lengthens the vowel before it and has a soft buzz; /s/ shortens the vowel and ends with a crisp hiss. In final position the buzz can be weak, so vowel length is the most reliable cue.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold the tongue behind the upper teeth. For /s/ end with a sharp hiss after a short vowel; for /z/ stretch the vowel and finish with a softer buzz.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Both words fit the phrase. Focus on the first sound: touch or curl?
quests.explanation: In this phrase, "lamb" started with the tongue tip touching the ridge. "Ram" starts with a curl and no contact.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /l/ is made with the tongue tip touching the ridge behind the upper teeth, letting air flow around the sides; British /r/ is made with the tongue tip curled slightly back and not touching anything, often with lips a little rounded.
quests.mouthPosition: For /l/ press the tongue tip firmly against the ridge behind the upper teeth. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep it away from the roof of the mouth, lips slightly rounded.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The first sound is either voiced or voiceless. Which do you catch through the phrase?
quests.explanation: It was "joke": a voiced, buzzing start. "Choke" starts breathier and sharper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /tʃ/ and /dʒ/ share the same tongue movement; /tʃ/ is voiceless and /dʒ/ is voiced. The voiced version has a buzz and a longer preceding vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: Press the tongue against the ridge behind the teeth and release into a hush. Keep the throat silent for /tʃ/; add voice for /dʒ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: In a two-syllable word, listen to the strong first syllable.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "pedal" had a half-open, crisp vowel. "Paddle" opens wider and sounds fuller.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are front vowels, but /æ/ is lower. That extra openness makes /æ/ sound wider and slightly longer than the crisp, short /e/.
quests.mouthPosition: Place a finger under your chin: the jaw should drop noticeably more for /æ/ than for /e/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The word is followed by a weak "of" or "on". Listen to how it ends.
quests.explanation: What you caught was "tug": the vowel lingered a moment and the ending was soft and voiced. "Tuck" ends crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The clearest cue is vowel length: longer before /ɡ/, shorter before /k/.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel slightly before /ɡ/ and clip it before /k/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Lips or tongue? Listen to the very start of the stressed word.
quests.explanation: This time, "wage" began with rounded lips gliding open. "Rage" begins with a curled tongue.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /w/ starts with strongly rounded lips that spread open; /r/ starts with the tongue tip pulled back.
quests.mouthPosition: Let the tongue tip stay down for /w/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: One vowel is steady and one glides. Which one?
quests.explanation: That was "hall": a steady rounded vowel with no slide. "Hole" starts relaxed and rounds off.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are long enough to notice. Ask yourself whether the vowel holds the same shape throughout (/ɔː/) or changes shape (/əʊ/).
quests.mouthPosition: Say /ɔː/ with a tall, round mouth held still; say /əʊ/ starting relaxed and closing the lips.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the start carry a puff of air?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "time" began with a breathy release from the tongue tip. "Dime" starts with the voice on straight away.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voice onset time separates them: /t/ delays it, /d/ starts it immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Keep the tongue tip firm on the ridge for /t/ and a little softer for /d/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Forget the vowel. Is the opening a thin, high hiss or a broader, lower hush?
quests.explanation: You heard "sign": a thin, sharp hiss with spread lips. "Shine" starts with a broader hush and rounded lips.
quests.vowelTensionRule: The lips and tongue position both differ, and together they change the colour of the noise.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch your lips: they push forward for /ʃ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how wide the vowel is inside the stressed word.
quests.explanation: Here, "mess" had a half-open vowel. "Mass" is wider and a bit longer.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /e/ is a short mid-front vowel with the jaw only half open; /æ/ is more open and a little longer, with the jaw dropped and the tongue lowered at the front.
quests.mouthPosition: For /e/ open the jaw about halfway and keep the lips relaxed. For /æ/ drop the jaw further and spread the mouth slightly, as if beginning to yawn sideways.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to where the vowel begins: half open, or wide open?
quests.explanation: It was "pain": the vowel started at half open and glided a short way. "Pine" opens wide first.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are diphthongs that end in the same place, so listen to the beginning: open and low (/aɪ/) or mid (/eɪ/).
quests.mouthPosition: The glide is longer in /aɪ/ because the jaw starts lower.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the very first burst of the stressed word.
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "bunch" opened with a soft, voiced release. "Punch" opens with a breath of air.
quests.vowelTensionRule: At the start of a word, /p/ is released with a small puff of air (aspiration) and no vocal-fold vibration; /b/ has little or no puff and voicing starts almost immediately.
quests.mouthPosition: Close both lips. For /p/ release them with a clear burst of air; for /b/ release them gently and start the vowel immediately.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Two diphthongs. Which one starts rounded?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "owl": the mouth started open and ended rounded. "Oil" starts rounded and ends spread.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ɔɪ/ begins with a rounded back vowel and glides up to /ɪ/, so it has a distinctive 'oh-ee' movement that neither of its competitors share.
quests.mouthPosition: Start with the lips rounded and the tongue back, then slide the tongue forward and up while the lips spread.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.textToSpeak: There's a rag on the floor.
quests.hint: The ending is either soft or crisp. Also check the length of the vowel before it.
quests.explanation: This time, "rag" had a slightly longer vowel and a soft ending. "Rack" is crisper.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Word-final /ɡ/ is often partly devoiced in British English, so don't wait for the buzz; measure the vowel.
quests.mouthPosition: The back of the tongue rises to the soft palate in both; only the timing differs.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the final sound: airy or sharp?
quests.explanation: That was "tenth": the ending was a soft, airy /θ/ with the tongue at the teeth. "Tense" finishes with a sharp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /θ/ sounds soft and diffuse; /s/ sounds sharp and high-pitched.
quests.mouthPosition: Look in a mirror: you should see the tongue tip for /θ/ but not for /s/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: After the /b/, is there contact or curl?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "braid" curled the tongue back after the /b/. "Blade" touches the ridge with the tongue tip.
quests.vowelTensionRule: In a consonant cluster the /l/ or /r/ follows another consonant, so the difference is smaller. /l/ needs tongue contact at the ridge; /r/ needs a curled tongue tip and often shortens or devoices the first consonant slightly.
quests.mouthPosition: Say the first consonant, then for /l/ touch the tongue tip to the ridge, for /r/ curl it back without touching.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Same start and ending. How long is the vowel?
quests.explanation: The word was "cheek": a long, tense vowel. "Chick" clips short.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /iː/ is long and tense with the tongue high and forward; /ɪ/ is short, loose and a little lower and more central. Length and tension travel together, so a stretched vowel usually means /iː/.
quests.mouthPosition: For /iː/ spread the lips as if smiling and lift the tongue high behind the lower teeth. For /ɪ/ let the lips relax and drop the tongue a touch.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: The start is either lip-led or tongue-led.
quests.explanation: Here, "won" started with rounded lips and no tongue movement. "Run" starts with the tongue curling back.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /w/ is a lip glide: the lips round and open while the back of the tongue rises; /r/ is a tongue glide: the tip curls back with only slight lip rounding.
quests.mouthPosition: For /w/ push the lips into a tight round then open quickly into the vowel. For /r/ curl the tongue tip back and keep the lips relaxed.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the vowel length and the ending buzz or hiss.
quests.explanation: You heard "phase": a longer vowel and a buzzing ending. "Face" is shorter and hisses.
quests.vowelTensionRule: A longer vowel signals /z/; a shorter vowel and a strong hiss signal /s/.
quests.mouthPosition: Feel your throat vibrate through the end of /z/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: At the end of the word, how long does the vowel last?
quests.explanation: In the sentence, "bead" stretched the vowel and closed softly. "Beat" is shorter and ends crisply.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both end on the same tongue position, but the voiced /d/ lengthens the preceding vowel while /t/ clips it.
quests.mouthPosition: Stretch the vowel before /d/; cut it short before /t/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Does the start carry a breathy release?
quests.explanation: What you caught was "ghost": a soft voiced start. "Coast" opens with a puff of air.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Initial /k/ has a strong puff of air and is voiceless; /ɡ/ has very little puff and voicing starts quickly. Both are made at the back of the tongue.
quests.mouthPosition: Raise the back of the tongue to the soft palate. Release with a puff of air for /k/; with a soft, voiced release for /ɡ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Compare the opening sound: broad hush or thin hiss?
quests.explanation: This time, "shore" began with a broad hush and rounded lips. "Sore" starts with a sharp hiss.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /ʃ/ is a broader, lower-pitched hush made with the tongue pulled slightly back and the lips a little rounded; /s/ is a sharper, higher hiss with the tongue tip near the teeth and the lips spread.
quests.mouthPosition: For /ʃ/ round the lips slightly and pull the tongue back so the air flows over a wider channel. For /s/ spread the lips and bring the tongue tip close to the ridge behind your teeth.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to how wide the mouth is when the vowel begins.
quests.explanation: That was "pile": the mouth opened wide before closing. "Pale" starts half open.
quests.vowelTensionRule: /aɪ/ sounds like it begins with a bigger mouth opening.
quests.mouthPosition: Watch the jaw: a big movement for /aɪ/, a smaller one for /eɪ/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Puff of breath at the start, or none?
quests.explanation: In this phrase "bride" began with a soft, voiced lip release. "Pride" begins with a breathy pop.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Both are lip stops. The cue is the puff: strong for /p/, weak for /b/. Hold a hand or a tissue in front of your mouth and feel the difference.
quests.mouthPosition: Hold a tissue in front of your lips: it should flutter for /p/ but hardly move for /b/.

quests.instruction: Listen to the phrase, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the ending: voiceless hush or voiced buzz?
quests.explanation: The word was "batch": a breathy /tʃ/ after a shorter vowel. "Badge" has a voiced /dʒ/ and a slightly longer vowel.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Voicing is the only change; listen for the buzz in /dʒ/.
quests.mouthPosition: Touch the throat to feel the vibration.

quests.instruction: Listen carefully, then select the word you hear.
quests.hint: Listen to the first sound before the long vowel.
quests.explanation: "raw" began with a curled tongue, and there was no contact. "Law" taps the ridge.
quests.vowelTensionRule: Contact versus no contact: /l/ touches the ridge; /r/ hovers below it.
quests.mouthPosition: If your tongue touches the roof, you are making /l/; if it doesn't, /r/.
